# Session 2 — bed scheduler, central office (synthetic)

Interviewer: What does your morning look like?
Dr. Patel: I'm not clinical despite the title joke — I run scheduling. Mornings are triage: forty discharge predictions, half wrong. The system says a bed frees at 11, the floor says the patient hasn't seen physical therapy yet.
Interviewer: Where does the prediction come from?
Dr. Patel: An algorithm nobody trusts. Nurses pad estimates so they don't get blamed; the algorithm learns the padding. I spend two hours a day on the phone reconciling. I keep my own spreadsheet — that spreadsheet is the real system of record, which terrifies me.
Interviewer: What about the status board the units use?
Dr. Patel: Different system, different vendor, syncs every thirty minutes on a good day. The Dayton campus is worse — they're on the older version.
Interviewer: Magic wand?
Dr. Patel: Kill the spreadsheet. Give me one queue where the floor updates status once and everyone — transport, environmental services, me — sees the same thing at the same second.
